clue.text: Very senior citizen laps up our flattery

indicators.note: to lap something up is to take it in eagerly, so the words around it swallow the other piece

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
OAP, old-age pensioner, is the British term for a senior citizen
the clue appears in the Financial Times, so 'our' is the FT's, written FTS

explanation.surface: An elderly person happily soaks up the compliments we pay them.
explanation.walkthrough: In an FT puzzle 'our' points to the paper itself, the FT; the possessive gives FTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-soap is smooth, insincere praise used to win someone over, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Where restaurants may be beset by some pernicious, primarily bovine disease

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded, so the shopping centre sits inside the other letters
primarily picks out the first letters of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of some and pernicious
an ox is a bovine animal
food outlets cluster in a shopping mall

explanation.surface: Eateries are hit by a nasty disease that began with cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: Smallpox's link to cattle is real: the vaccine came from cowpox.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallpox is a contagious viral illness, eradicated in 1980.

clue.text: In time Foucault displaced to and fro motion

indicators.note: displaced means moved out of position, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the physicist's name supplies its letters as written

explanation.surface: Over time, Foucault's famous pendulum swung back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: Foucault's pendulum, swinging to and fro, demonstrates the Earth's rotation, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluctuation is a rise and fall or swing between values, a back-and-forth movement.

clue.text: Perhaps Virginia intended to ignore article furnishing account?

parts.note: Virginia is an example of a US state

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out

parts.note: meant is a synonym for intended
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Was a US state meant to overlook an item in its financial report?
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a written report or description, as in a bank statement or witness's version.

clue.text: Serve rhubarb extremely sour

parts.note: an ace is a serve the opponent cannot return in tennis

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of rhubarb

explanation.surface: A cook serves up rhubarb that is very tart.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is an adjective meaning bitter or sharp-tasting, like acerbic.

clue.text: One state ceding frontier right to another

indicators.note: to cede is to give up territory, so these letters are surrendered from the state's name

parts.note: Arkansas is a US state
the frontier of the state's name is its front letter

explanation.surface: A US state hands over its border land to a neighbouring state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frontier' is read as front-ier: the first letter of the state named, which goes along with R.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a second, separate US state, so it is simply another one besides the first.

clue.text: Modify flat that's on the way up in centre of Bath

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other
the centre of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: the two middle letters of the city's name

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: pad is slang for a flat or home

explanation.surface: Someone alters a flat in a rising part of central Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city; here only its middle letters count. Pad is informal for a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to alter it to suit new conditions.

clue.text: Telecoms company achieving 75pc coverage in island

indicators.note: covering three quarters of a four-letter word means keeping three letters and losing the last

parts.note: Skye is an island of the Scottish Hebrides

explanation.surface: A broadband firm reaches three quarters of homes on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British broadcaster and phone provider; Skye is in the Inner Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky is a major British satellite TV, broadband and mobile provider.

clue.text: Odds on horse possessing little range

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so the outer letters hold the inner ones

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds at which a horse starts a race
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: Betting on a horse with a short range of form.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the bookmakers' term for a horse's final odds.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweep is a broad expanse or scope, as in the sweep of a view.

clue.text: Most crushing resistance shown by first and second individuals on the left

indicators.note: crushing something means pressing it in the grip of another, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the most
1st written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: The fiercest opposition comes from the leading two people on the political left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' is 1ST with the numeral as Roman I.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxists, followers of Karl Marx, are socialists and communists on the political left.

clue.text: Lavish praise on a university student admitted to appointment

parts.note: the article taken as written

indicators.note: letters admitted to another word are let inside it

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting
L is a learner, the plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A student given a place at a university gets showered with compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to flatter or admire someone excessively, heaping praise upon them.

clue.text: Examine animal outside centre gypsies used regularly

indicators.note: only the outside of the word is kept, its centre letters thrown away

parts.note: the word as written, before its centre goes

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of gypsies

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a creature found beyond a centre run by travellers.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something is to study it in detail, breaking it down to examine it.

clue.text: Front door opening without keys? Spooner suggests what's needed

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words here trade their first sounds

parts.note: with no keys, the obvious need is better security, so the phrase sought is better locks
a door that can be opened without keys needs better locks

explanation.surface: A householder who can get in without keys wonders what's needed to make the front door secure.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase wanted is 'better locks'; said with the opening sounds swapped it comes out as the answer, LOCKS heard as LOX.
explanation.definitionFit: A letterbox is the slot in a front door through which post is pushed, an opening in it.

clue.text: Supply more drink where Labour leads in Labrador

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to refill a glass
second meaning: LAB, short for Labour, stands at the top of the word Labrador, so it is ...

explanation.surface: A barman refills glasses at a gathering where the Labour Party is ahead in Labrador.
explanation.walkthrough: LAB is the usual short form of Labour; it sits at the very start, top and up, of the word LABRADOR in a down-read sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up a glass is to fill it again with more drink.

clue.text: Act well in drama on prostitution

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the other

parts.note: a play is a drama
'the game' is British slang for prostitution, as in being on the game

explanation.surface: A stage drama about selling sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the game' is British slang for working as a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: To play the game is an idiom for behaving fairly and honourably.

clue.text: Some Americans love Rishi

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a rishi is a Hindu sage or seer

explanation.surface: Some Americans are fond of a politician called Rishi.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi looks like a first name (Rishi Sunak); it is the Sanskrit word for a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains, so they are some Americans.

clue.text: Key operative making notes in bars?

definitions.meaning: sounds like an important agent, but a key is a musical key and the operative works in it
sounds like a spy jotting things down in pubs; really playing musical notes within bars of music

explanation.surface: A vital secret agent jots down intelligence while sitting in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer playing in a key produces notes grouped into bars, which is what a player of music does.

clue.text: He projected car workers' schedule falling back

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes car

indicators.note: falling back means going in reverse, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of work shifts

explanation.surface: A car plant's shift timetable slips behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projected' points to the map projection named after him, not a forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercator, a Flemish cartographer, devised the map projection that bears his name.

clue.text: Could this require putting up with obstacles in the way of wordplay for 'flog'?

definitions.text: Could this require putting up with obstacles
definitions.meaning: the game involves putting a ball around windmills and other obstacles, and 'putting up with' reads as tolerating

definitions.text: in the way of wordplay for 'flog'
definitions.meaning: in crossword wordplay, a 'crazy' version of one word is an anagram, and flog jumbled gives the second word of the answer

explanation.surface: Does something mean enduring hindrances, like obstacles in the path of a clue about flogging?
explanation.definitionFit: This is a novelty putting game played round obstacles such as windmills and ramps.

clue.text: May such pieces provide one with a taster in performance?

definitions.text: May such pieces provide one with a taster in performance?

indicators.note: letters put in performance are acted out in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Might these short works give a listener a sample during a concert?
explanation.definitionFit: Ariettas are short, light arias, small vocal pieces that give a brief taste of song.

clue.text: They boom in Nova Scotia after a beer

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer

parts.note: bitter is a type of British beer
NS is the postal abbreviation for the Canadian province

explanation.surface: People get loud in Nova Scotia after drinking a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They boom' suggests rowdy drinkers; it is the booming call of a wading bird. Bitter is a British pale ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitterns are marsh herons famous for their deep, foghorn-like booming call.

clue.text: First-magnitude star I omitted in table

indicators.note: something omitted is left out, so the letter is dropped from the star's name

parts.note: Altair, in Aquila, is one of the brightest stars
the letter as written in the clue

explanation.surface: A very bright star is missing from an astronomical table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' looks like a chart of stars; it is the communion table in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An altar is the raised table in a church at which the Eucharist is celebrated.

clue.text: Naval officer exchanges points for more money

indicators.note: points of the compass, S and N, swap places, rearranging the letters

parts.note: a bosun is a ship's petty officer in charge of equipment

explanation.surface: A navy officer trades in his medals or points for extra cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The points are the compass letters S and N in the officer's title, which change places.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra payment on top of normal pay, so it is additional cash.

clue.text: Soprano in lingerie displaying cheek

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: bras are items of lingerie

explanation.surface: A singer in underwear shows off her backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheek' looks like a bottom; it means impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is informal for nerve or impudence, as in brass neck.

clue.text: Writer doesn't finish either half of hardback

indicators.note: the last letter of the writer's name is left off

parts.note: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy

explanation.surface: An author fails to complete either half of a hardback book.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'hardback' into hard and back: the answer means both, severe and the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern can mean hard, or strict, and also the back of a vessel, so it fits each half.

clue.text: Suspect girl's not involved in energetically dispersing gas

indicators.note: suspect means not to be trusted as given, so the removed letters come in any order
is not involved means those letters take no part, so they are taken out
dispersing scatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A dubious girl is kept out of the energetic spreading of some gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Take G, I, R, L out of ENERGETICALLY and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylene is a flammable hydrocarbon gas used in welding torches.

clue.text: Went wrong under-reporting uprising to some extent

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read from the bottom upwards
only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of under and reporting

explanation.surface: Officials blundered by playing down a revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Erred is the past tense of err, to make a mistake.

clue.text: No pressure for division of French company to display style

indicators.note: no pressure means the letter for pressure is removed

parts.note: a part is a section or division
de is French for of

explanation.surface: A French firm splits off a division to show off a stress-free style.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is a decorative design style of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Scour bottom of lake for sailor

indicators.note: scouring clears something away, here the last letter of the word

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

explanation.surface: Search the lakebed for a missing seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scour' looks like 'search'; it means scrub off, here the lake's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar, from tarpaulin, is an old informal word for a seaman.

clue.text: Ricotta conformed to statutory provision

indicators.note: to be conformed is to be reshaped to fit, so the cheese's letters take a new form

parts.note: the cheese's name supplies its letters as written

explanation.surface: A soft cheese was made to meet the law's requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was a British statute of 1714; reading it ordered a crowd to disperse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riot Act was an actual law, a legal statute, whose reading compelled crowds to break up.

clue.text: Withdrew direction to be silent order

parts.note: sh is the instruction to be quiet
a rank is a grade or order in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: Someone backed off after being ordered to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrank, as in shrank back, means recoiled or retreated from something.

clue.text: Bogus fireside gurus

indicators.note: bogus means fake, so the letters are false and need rearranging

parts.note: the word as written supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Fake wise men hold forth by the hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Edifiers are those who instruct and improve others morally or intellectually, as teachers do.
